clue.text: Ordered ace, perhaps, to be entered for this race

indicators.note: ordered means arranged afresh, so the letters of the two words beside it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is enrolling a top player, perhaps, in a particular race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' looks like 'entered on someone's orders' but signals rearranging ACE PERHAPS; 'to be entered for this' links the letters to the race they spell.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper chase is a cross-country run where hares lay a trail of paper scraps for the hounds to follow.

clue.text: In reduced circumstances, old man's embarrassed

parts.note: old man is slang for father, pa
an embarrassed person goes red

explanation.surface: Dad is mortified to have fallen on hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: Pared means cut back or trimmed down, so reduced to less.

clue.text: Cut parole arranged for robber

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thief's early release on licence was fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' reworks CUT PAROLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A peculator embezzles funds, stealing money entrusted to them.

clue.text: One offers vision of what may come to pass

definitions.text: One offers vision of what may come to pass

parts.words: One offers vision of what may come to pass
parts.note: sounds like a prophet foreseeing the future, but describes a driver's glass showing traffic about to overtake

explanation.definitionFit: This glass lets a driver see vehicles behind that may overtake.

clue.text: Some rhymes are uninspiring

definitions.meaning: the two halves of the word chime with each other, a rhyming pair

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a reduplicated rhyming pair meaning dull and monotonous.

clue.text: In two ways, a major honour for celebrity

indicators.note: in means the following letter sits inside the two pieces placed side by side

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
RD is short for road, another way
OM is the Order of Merit, a major British honour

explanation.surface: Fame is a top award in more than one sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In two ways' pretends to mean 'in two senses'; 'In' is really the container signal, and both ways are abbreviations for street and road.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardom is the status of being a famous performer, celebrity itself.

clue.text: Elegant yellow in which Ken's turned out

indicators.note: turned out means evicted, so the name Ken is thrown out of the longer word that holds it

parts.note: yellow means cowardly, which is chicken
the name Ken, with 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A stylish yellow outfit that Ken has dressed up in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned out' pretends to mean 'dressed', but it signals removing KEN from CHICKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a borrowed French word for stylish and fashionable.

clue.text: Throw Satan finally out of Paradise

indicators.note: out of means the letter is ejected from the word for paradise

parts.note: Paradise is heaven

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of Satan

explanation.surface: Milton-like scene of the devil hurled from Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of Satan, N, is thrown out of HEAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to hurl or throw something heavy.

clue.text: Purge of sect members is to follow

indicators.note: to follow means the little word comes after the sect name

parts.note: the Cathars were a medieval heretical Christian sect in southern France

explanation.surface: A religious group is about to clear out its membership.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is a cleansing or purging, of emotions or of the body.

clue.text: A tiny contribution made by American astronauts finally

definitions.meaning: an amount too small to make any difference
Apollo capsules ended their missions by splashing down into the sea

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a negligible amount, and literally describes a capsule splashing into the sea.

clue.text: Sort of miracle recovery

definitions.note: a noun, matching the noun use of the answer, as in baggage reclaim

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to arrange, so the letters of miracle are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's recovery from illness is little short of a miracle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' reads as 'kind of' but is the instruction to rearrange MIRACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reclaim as a noun is the act of getting something back, as at an airport's baggage reclaim.

clue.text: Conversant with what was lost by the Amazon

definitions.meaning: being up to date with, as in keeping level with the news

definitions.text: what was lost by the Amazon
definitions.meaning: legend says the Amazon warrior women removed one breast to draw a bow more easily

explanation.surface: A riddle about knowing what the Amazon warrior gave up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Amazon' suggests the river, but it is one of the legendary female warriors; split the answer as A BREAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping abreast of something means staying informed and familiar with it.

clue.text: Born free

definitions.meaning: a baby is brought into the world by birth

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both brought forth at birth and rescued, released from captivity.

clue.text: Sacred sculpture showing two Greek characters

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
eta is another letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A religious statue displays a couple of figures from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek characters' suggests people from Greece, but means letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a sculpture or painting of the Virgin Mary holding the dead body of Christ, Michelangelo's being the most famous.

clue.text: Handle book for publisher

definitions.meaning: a handle is slang for a name or form of address
publishers speak of each book on their list as an individual item they publish

explanation.definitionFit: A title is both the name or rank someone is addressed by and, in publishing, a single book on the list.

clue.text: Check striker is okay for big game

parts.note: to check is to test
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: An inspector says the forward is fit for the important fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striker' suggests a footballer, but it is a match that strikes. A test match is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A test match is a full international fixture, usually in cricket, a major sporting occasion.

clue.text: Times covering university — that's significant

indicators.note: covering means one word wraps round and encloses the other one

parts.note: times are moments, as in 'at moments like these'
OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university

explanation.surface: A newspaper's coverage of a university is said to matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' tempts as the newspaper, and 'covering' as reporting on; the university here is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning institution.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentous is of great importance or consequence.

clue.text: A cello —- it's playing swing

indicators.note: playing suggests moving freely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cellist's instrument is played in swing style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' reworks A CELLO ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to swing back and forth regularly.

clue.text: Footballer, namely, having a couple of drinks

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely
rum is one drink
a half is a half-pint of beer, a second drink

explanation.surface: A footballer, it turns out, has had a couple of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: A scrum-half is a rugby player; rugby is a football code, so 'Footballer' is fair. A half is British pub talk for half a pint.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrum-half is the rugby union player who feeds the ball into the scrum, rugby being one form of football.

clue.text: A politician in US enters one place of learning

indicators.note: enters means the first pieces go inside the word for one

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards and dice
Dem is short for a Democrat, a US politician

explanation.surface: An American politician takes up a place at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' seems to go with 'place of learning', but it is ACE, which takes in A DEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the world of universities and scholarship, the academy.

clue.text: Sort of conspiracy case appearing for trial

parts.note: a frame is a case or casing round something
someone up before the court is appearing for trial

explanation.surface: A plot whose case is coming to court.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame-up is a plot to make an innocent person look guilty.

clue.text: Picks horses

definitions.meaning: a hack is a pick or mattock, a tool for breaking ground
horses for ordinary riding, or hired horses

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both rough cutting tools like pickaxes and plain horses for hire or everyday riding.

clue.text: A large bird, some say, that keeps the grass down

indicators.note: some say means the bird's name is heard spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: the moa is a large extinct flightless bird of New Zealand

explanation.surface: A big bird that some claim grazes the lawn short.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech, with no sounded R, the bird's name and the answer sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is the machine used to cut lawns short.

clue.text: Sound delighted as Health Authority's laid on operation

indicators.note: laid on means, in a down clue, the first piece is placed on top of the second

parts.note: WHO is the World Health Organization, a health authority

explanation.surface: A patient cheers because the health service has arranged surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid on' looks like 'provided', but in a down clue it stacks the health body above the surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud cry of joy or excitement.

clue.text: Religious leader always greeting army on return

parts.note: ay, or aye, is an old word for always or ever

indicators.note: on return means the two words before it are read from end to start together

parts.note: hallo is a greeting
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve army

explanation.surface: A cleric keeps saluting the troops as they come home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' turns the greeting and the army together into ATOLLAH; the Territorial Army is Britain's volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shiite Muslim cleric in Iran.

clue.text: One was bound to land something from the lottery

indicators.note: something from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A winner was sure to get something from the draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to land' reads as 'certain to win', but means tied to the soil, a serf.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf in ancient Sparta, tied to the land he worked.

clue.text: Sergeant-majors seen in volume, but not quite a crowd, they say

definitions.text: not quite a crowd, they say

indicators.note: seen in means the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: a tome is a large volume or book
a sergeant-major is a warrant officer, WO, so the plural gives WOS

explanation.surface: Senior army sergeants appear in a book, though there are too few to form a mob.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying 'two's company, three's a crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is company; the proverb says only a trio makes a crowd.

clue.text: Eastern potentate rejected everything in sphere of vision

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the ruler's title is read backwards

parts.note: a bey was a Turkish governor or ruler
everything means all

explanation.surface: An oriental ruler refuses everything within view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns BEY into YEB.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe-shaped organ of sight is literally a sphere used for seeing.

clue.text: Indians one associates with dance

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Native Americans whom one links with dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hopi are a Native American people of northeast Arizona.

clue.text: Needs desperately to swallow water to get last of tablet down

indicators.note: to swallow means the jumbled letters take in the next word whole
desperately suggests wild disorder, so the letters of needs are scrambled

parts.note: a pond is a body of water

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of tablet is used

explanation.surface: A patient in need gulps water to wash the last pill down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' rearranges the first word to DESEN, which 'to swallow' wraps round the water before the tablet's last letter ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling down means being low in spirits, dejected.
